row: | DOC-A.1-128 | **OCCURS clause — range of values allowed in the index**, §13.18.38.4 GR2, required + documented | **The full signed 64-bit interval, −9 223 372 036 854 775 808 through +9 223 372 036 854 775 807.** In this data model an index IS its 1-based occurrence number, held in a C# `long` (each INDEXED BY name is an `IndexDeclaration` owning its own `long` cell, minted by `DataBinder.RegisterIndexes`; COBOLNET_DATA_MODEL_DESIGN D3), so the allowed range is that carrier's range — `CobolIndex.MinIndex` / `CobolIndex.MaxIndex`. §13.18.38.4 GR2 requires the range to include at least occurrence numbers (1 − integer-2) through (2 × integer-2); integer-2 cannot exceed this implementation's maximum occurrence count (`CobolDynTable.MaxOccurrences`, 2^30−1), so the required interval is contained with more than thirty bits to spare. ⛔ **A value inside the range but outside the TABLE is not out of range**: §14.9.39.4 GR2 a) 1. c and GR4 b) each end "even if that occurrence is not a valid occurrence within this table", so an index pointing past its own table is legal and must not raise — a table-bounds test here would reject conforming programs. GR2's own three statements enforce the range (kb/Work PB459): a SET amount lands through `CobolIndex.TryAmount` and a SET / PERFORM VARYING augment through `CobolIndex.Augment`, each of which sets EC-RANGE-INDEX and leaves the index unchanged on a value or result outside it (GR2 b's "undefined unless the value of the index is specified by the rules of that statement" — §14.9.39.4 GR2 a) 1. b and GR4 a) specify it, so it is not undefined). A SEARCH cannot reach the boundary at all: §14.9.37.4 GR4's initial-index guard leaves the scan only when the index is within the table's occurrence count, so its `+= 1` is bounded by that count. | `conformance:2023/pb459_set_index_amount_guards`; `conformance:2023/pb459_set_index_amount_ec`; `conformance:2002/pb459_set_index_range_ec`; `conformance:85/pb459_set_index_overflow_unchanged` |

row: | DOC-A.1-130 | **OPEN statement with the OUTPUT phrase — positioning of the output file with regard to physical page boundaries**, §14.9.27.4 GR18, required + documented | Physical pages have meaning for a **sequential-organization** file (record sequential or LINE SEQUENTIAL) — the files WRITE ... ADVANCING and the LINAGE clause apply to; a relative or indexed file has no pages. **OPEN OUTPUT creates the host file empty and places the output medium at its first byte, which is the TOP OF THE FIRST PHYSICAL PAGE.** The OPEN itself writes nothing — no form feed, no blank lines, no margin: a file opened OUTPUT and closed with no WRITE is **0 bytes** (`SequentialConnector.OpenWriter`). **No LINAGE clause:** because the medium is already at a page top, the first `WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING PAGE` (or BEFORE) still repositions to the NEXT physical page as §14.9.51.4 GR25 h) says, by writing a form feed (U+000C) — so a file whose first WRITE advances PAGE begins with a form feed (`SequentialConnector.Advance`). **LINAGE clause:** at the completion of the OPEN the device is on line 1 of the first logical page, and that logical page begins at the file's first line; LINAGE-COUNTER is 1 (§13.18.34.4 GR7). The logical page's TOP margin lines are written onto the medium immediately before the first record is presented — never by the OPEN, so a LINAGE file closed with no WRITE is also 0 bytes (`SequentialConnector.BeginLinagePage`, `EmitTopMarginIfPending`). Example: `FD F LINAGE 5 FOOTING 4 TOP 2 BOTTOM 1`, OPEN OUTPUT, one plain `WRITE` of `AAA` gives two empty lines, then `AAA` (line terminator per item 114). Same in every edition. | `conformance:2023/pb523_linage_margins_on_the_medium`; `conformance:85/pb523_linage_margins_on_the_medium_85` |

record.notes: §14.9.27.4 GR18 (cite.py OK §14.9.27.4 18)) leaves positioning with respect to physical page boundaries to the implementor; COBOL.NET's answer is 'top of the first physical page, nothing written by the OPEN'. Verified in code: OpenWriter(FileMode.Create) writes nothing; BeginLinagePage (SequentialConnector.cs:497) sets LinageCounter = 1 and _topMarginPending, materialized by EmitTopMarginIfPending before the first presentation; Advance (L1170) writes '\f' for ADVANCING PAGE on a non-LINAGE file. Probes probe/pg.cob --std 2023 (LINAGE-COUNTER after OPEN = 0001; LINAGE file with one WRITE = CRLF CRLF AAA CRLF; LINAGE file with no WRITE = 0 bytes; line-sequential and record-sequential first WRITE AFTER ADVANCING PAGE = \f then the record) and probe/pg85.cob --std 85 (same bytes). The pb523 goldens pin the LINAGE half (page 1 begins at the file's first physical line, top margin on the medium); the non-LINAGE form-feed half has no golden. This row discharges determination D of kb/Work PB322 (open; its other determinations A/B/C/E/F stay open).

row: | DOC-A.1-132 | **MODULE-NAME function — which type of dynamic-length elementary item is the returned value**, §15.65.4 r1, conditionally required + documented | COBOL.NET supports more than one type of dynamic-length elementary item — alphanumeric and national, each either with the implementor-defined internal structure (no dynamic-length-structure-name, §8.5.1.10.2) or with a PREFIXED / DELIMITED structure named by a DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE clause (determination D-DL3 in §3) — so r1 requires the choice to be stated. **MODULE-NAME returns an ALPHANUMERIC dynamic-length elementary item with the implementor-defined internal structure** — the same type as a `PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH` item that names no dynamic-length-structure-name: a native .NET `System.String`, one character per character position, whose maximum size is the implementor maximum of item 62 (1,073,741,791 characters). It is never national and never a PREFIXED or DELIMITED structure, so no PREFIXED length-field bound (65535 / 32767) applies to it. The value is exactly the name, with no trailing spaces (item 133): `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MODULE-NAME(CURRENT))` in program `MNPROG` is 6, ACTIVATING in a main program is one space (length 1). Implemented as the `MODULE-NAME` entry of `IntrinsicCatalog` (result type alphanumeric), evaluated by `CobolModule.Name`. COBOL 2023 only — the function does not exist in earlier editions (COBOLNET1502). | — |

record.notes: §15.65.4 r1 (cite.py OK §15.65.4 1)) requires the type to be documented when more than one type of dynamic-length elementary item is supported; §8.5.1.10.2 (cite.py --find) makes the structure either implementor-defined or named by a DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE clause, and COBOL.NET supports both plus both classes (D-DL3, DOC-A.1-62), so the condition holds. Code: IntrinsicCatalog.cs:328 registers MODULE-NAME with IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric; CobolModule.Name(int) returns a System.String (the carrier of a structure-less DYNAMIC LENGTH item). No golden or unit test pins the type (ModuleStackInvariantTests pins item 133's no-trailing-spaces), so Pinned by is honestly empty. Incidental: BYTE-LENGTH(FUNCTION MODULE-NAME(CURRENT)) is refused with a COBOLNET1627 message calling the argument a numeric literal - already owned by kb/Work PB1068. Previously the substance sat only in DOC-A.1-133's cell.

row: | DOC-A.1-138 | **Parameterized classes and interfaces — manner and time of expansion**, §7.1 (with §12.3.8.4 GR5 / GR8), required + need not be documented (documented voluntarily) | **Time:** a parameterized class or interface is expanded at compile time, once per compilation group, AFTER all text manipulation — COPY, REPLACE and the compiler directives have finished, the source has been parsed, and expansion runs at the start of binding (`OoExpansion.Expand`, called from `BinderDriver`). So a REPLACE that produces a formal parameter's name inside the definition takes part in the substitution. **Manner:** each distinct expansion (`CLASS new-name EXPANDS definition USING actual …` or the interface form in a REPOSITORY paragraph) becomes an ORDINARY class or interface: the definition's own tokens re-parsed with every occurrence of each formal parameter replaced by its actual parameter (§12.3.8.4 GR5 / GR8) and the header renamed to the expansion's name. It is never a .NET generic type, and from binding onward an expansion cannot be told from a written class — its FACTORY and OBJECT data are its own (two expansions of one definition keep separate factory counters). The parameterized definition itself generates nothing. **Identity (§9.3.12):** specifiers that repeat one (expansion name, definition, actual parameters) triple, in one or several source elements, create ONE class; reusing an expansion name with a different definition or different actuals is **COBOLNET2240**. COBOL 2002 and later. | `conformance:2002/pb759_parameterized_class` |

row: | DOC-A.1-139 | **PERFORM statement — whether location information is available when the LOCATION phrase is not specified**, §14.9.28.4 GR14 (through §7.3.25.4 GR7), required + documented | **Not available.** An exception-checking PERFORM (Format 3, `PERFORM … WHEN exception-name …  END-PERFORM`) enables the exception conditions its WHEN phrases name over imperative-statement-1 through an implicit TURN directive (§14.9.28.4 GR14), and that implicit directive carries LOCATION exactly when the PERFORM writes `WITH LOCATION`. Without it COBOL.NET saves no location information for a condition raised there — the same determination as the explicit `>>TURN` directive (item 204), so neither route yields location data the other withholds. Consequence inside the WHEN handler and after the PERFORM: `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION` returns one alphanumeric space, `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N` one national space and `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT` 63 spaces, while `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS` still names the condition. With `PERFORM WITH LOCATION` the full location is produced — e.g. `PL; MAIN-P; 12` and statement `RAISE`. The LOCATION flag travels on `BoundExceptionPerform.WithLocation` into `TurnState.WithImplicitEnable`. COBOL 2023 only (Format 3 PERFORM is COBOLNET0900 in earlier editions). | `conformance:2023/l1_exception_no_location_arms`; `conformance:2023/exception_statement_ambient` |

record.notes: §14.9.28.4 GR14 (cite.py OK 14)) reads through to §7.3.25.4 GR7 (cite.py OK 7)); the substance was already stated under DOC-A.1-204 (TURN) and this row files it under item 139's own key. Verified: BoundExceptionPerform carries WithLocation into TurnState.WithImplicitEnable (TurnState.cs:93), and TurnState.WithLocation folds it per statement. Probe probe/pl.cob --std 2023: PERFORM ... RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-X1 WHEN EC-USER-X1 -> EXCEPTION-LOCATION [ ] and EXCEPTION-STATEMENT 63 spaces; PERFORM WITH LOCATION -> [PL; MAIN-P; 12] and RAISE; --std 2014 -> COBOLNET0900. No open note on this behaviour.

row: | DOC-A.1-141 | **Procedure division header rules when the activating or the activated runtime element is not COBOL — restrictions and mechanisms (parameter matching, data type representation, returning of a value, omission of parameters)**, §14.2.3 GR13, conditionally required + documented | **Supported non-COBOL language products: any .NET language, and only as the ACTIVATING element.** No non-COBOL element can be ACTIVATED: there is no CALL-CONVENTION directive (item 19), and a CALL, a program-pointer or `ADDRESS OF PROGRAM` resolves only COBOL.NET programs (otherwise EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND). **Mechanism:** every generated program class implements `ICobolProgram`, and a .NET host activates the program as a called program through `ICobolProgram.Call(CobolArg[] args, CobolArg? returning)`. **Parameter matching:** positional, `args[0]` to the first USING formal and so on (§14.2.3 GR2) — never by name. A trailing formal with no argument is OMITTED; an argument beyond the last formal is ignored; this entry performs no argument-count check (EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH for a count is raised only for a COBOL CALL, in `ProgramTable.CallProgram`). **Data type representation:** each argument is a `CobolArg(Mode, Carrier, Num, Layout)`. `Carrier` is a `ManagedPointer<T>` over the host's own storage: a `ManagedPointer<string>` holding the item's character image (one UTF-16 character per character position) for an alphanumeric, national, edited or group formal, or a native numeric cell (`long`, `Int128`, `double`, …) whose representation `Num` (a `NumProfile`: digits, scale, sign and usage) describes; `Layout` describes a group that contains a table. A formal of another shape sees the carrier through a converting view of the SAME storage (§14.2.3 GR8), so the program's stores reach the host's storage. `Mode` makes no copy: a COBOL CALL builds the BY CONTENT copy on the activating side, so a host that wants BY CONTENT passes a carrier over a copy it owns; a BY VALUE formal always adopts a detached copy (§14.2.3 GR10). A carrier the formal cannot read fails the activation with the .NET exception `CobolCallException` whose `EcName` is EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH, before any statement of the program runs (`CobolArgAdapt`). **Omission of parameters:** pass `ManagedPointer.Null` as the carrier, or pass fewer arguments; the omitted-argument condition is then true (§14.9.4.4 GR11), a reference raises EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED when checking for it is enabled in the program (GR12), and otherwise reads an empty value (zero for a numeric formal). **Returning of a value:** the RETURNING item's content is delivered into the `returning` argument's carrier, described by that `CobolArg` exactly as a COBOL receiver is; GOBACK / EXIT PROGRAM is an ordinary method return to the host (§3, "Return to a NON-COBOL activating runtime element"). Same in every edition. | — |

row: | DOC-A.1-143 | **Program-name — formation rules for a non-COBOL program**, §8.3.2.2.21, optional (documented if provided) | **Not provided.** COBOL.NET gives no program-name a non-COBOL meaning: there is no CALL-CONVENTION directive and no way to declare a non-COBOL program (item 19), so every program-name — in a CALL, a CANCEL, a program-pointer SET or `ADDRESS OF PROGRAM` — is formed and matched by the COBOL rules of §8.3.2.2 and resolves only to a COBOL.NET program. A name that happens to spell a non-COBOL module (e.g. `CALL "System.Console"`) is simply a program that is not found: EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, the CALL's ON EXCEPTION phrase, and a NULL program-pointer from `ADDRESS OF PROGRAM` (`ProgramTable.ProbeSiblingModule` accepts only a module that registers COBOL.NET programs). | — |

row: | DOC-A.1-148 | **RECORD clause — whether format 3 (`RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5`) produces fixed-length or variable-length records**, §13.18.43.4 GR17, required + documented | **Variable-length.** A file whose RECORD clause is format 3 has variable-length records in the range integer-4 through integer-5 bytes: each WRITE or REWRITE writes the record named in the statement at that record's own size, and a READ delivers the size that was written — records are NEVER padded to integer-5. On the medium each record carries the framing item 151 describes: record sequential, relative and indexed files write a 4-byte little-endian length prefix before each record, LINE SEQUENTIAL files end each record with a line delimiter. Example: `FD F3 RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 10 CHARACTERS` with `01 R3A PIC X(5)` and `01 R3B PIC X(10)`; writing R3A = `ABCDE` then R3B = `ABCDEFGHIJ` to a record sequential file gives the 23 bytes `05 00 00 00 'ABCDE' 0A 00 00 00 'ABCDEFGHIJ'`. Format 3 differs from format 2 (`RECORD IS VARYING …`) only where the standard ties a rule to the word VARYING — the READ INTO implicit move of §14.9.30.4 GR4 b) (`VaryingRecordInfo.VaryingClause`, set by `DataBinder.BindRecordClause`). Same in every edition. | — |

row: | DOC-A.1-153 | **Record locking — the default mode when the user specifies none**, §12.4.5.9.4 GR1 b) 2., required + documented | **No record locking** — the third option GR1 b) 2. names. A file connector whose file control entry has neither a LOCK MODE clause nor a SHARING clause, opened by an OPEN with no SHARING phrase, SETS NO RECORD LOCKS: a READ does not lock, and an explicit `WITH LOCK` phrase on its I-O statements obtains nothing (`FileRegistry.ImplementorDefaultShare`, lock mode `FileLockMode.None`). It still RESPECTS other connectors' locks, because §9.1.16 makes a locked record inaccessible to every other file connector: its READ, REWRITE and DELETE of a record another connector has locked are refused with I-O status `51`, and READ … IGNORING LOCK reads it. Example: two such connectors on one relative file — A `READ … WITH LOCK` record 1 (`00`), B READs and REWRITEs record 1 (`00`, `00`); a third connector with `LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC` READs record 1 and locks it, and B's next READ of record 1 is `51`. (The default SHARING mode of such a connector is item 131.) COBOL 2002 and later. | `conformance:2002/pb669_lock_visibility_plain_connector` |

row: | DOC-A.1-154 | **Record locking — the maximum number of record locks a run unit may hold**, §12.4.5.9.4 GR7, required + documented | **255** — the standard's minimum (`PhysicalFileTable.RunUnitLockMax`). The count is every record lock held by every file connector of the run unit, over all physical files. An I-O statement that would obtain a 256th lock is unsuccessful with I-O status **`53`** (§9.1.13.8 item 3) and obtains no lock; a WRITE or REWRITE refused this way changes no record (the ceiling is checked before the record is touched, `PhysicalFileTable.PreflightNewLock`). Re-locking a record the same connector already holds does not count again. When the connector's own ceiling (item 155) is also reached, `54` is reported. COBOL 2002 and later. | `unit:CobolFileLockTests.RunUnitLockLimit_256thRunUnitLock_Is53` |

row: | DOC-A.1-155 | **Record locks — the maximum number of record locks one file connector may hold**, §12.4.5.9.4 GR7, required + documented | **15** — the standard's minimum (`PhysicalFileTable.ConnectorLockMax`). Only a connector with multiple record locking (`LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS`) can hold more than one lock (GR6), and the MULTIPLE phrase is not allowed for sequential organization or access (§12.4.5.9.3 SR2), so the ceiling is reachable on relative and indexed files with random or dynamic access. An I-O statement that would obtain a 16th lock for the connector is unsuccessful with I-O status **`54`** (§9.1.13.8 item 4), obtains no lock and — for a READ — is an unsuccessful READ like any other (§14.9.30.4 GR18): no record position is established, so the next sequential READ is `46`, never the record after the refused one; a WRITE or REWRITE refused this way changes no record (`PhysicalFileTable.PreflightNewLock`). Re-locking a record the connector already holds does not count again; UNLOCK and CLOSE release its locks. COBOL 2002 and later. | `conformance:2023/pb338_read_lock_limit_position`; `unit:CobolFileLockTests.ConnectorLockLimit_16thRecord_Is54` |

record.notes: A.1 item 156 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 156): required + documented (A.1 cites 'Clause 6, Reference format, rule 3b'). §6.1: 'The implementor shall specify any control characters that terminate a free-form line' (cite.py --check 6.1 -> OK §6.1 b)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-156 row (the only reference-format row is DOC-A.1-158, margin R) and no prose elsewhere names the free-form line terminators. Code: NormalizeToFreeFormMapped splits the source on '\n' and each free-form segment line is TrimEnd('\r') (ReferenceFormatProcessor.cs:108/172), so LF terminates a line and a CR immediately before it is dropped; no other control character (FF, VT, lone CR) is a terminator. A fixed answer exists but is undocumented => DIVERGES, harm silent. Editions: free-form reference format exists from 2002 (Annex E). Owning note kb/Work PB1496 (open; its title names item 156 and its fixer owes the DOC-A.1-156 row) — cited, not re-reported. || Writer (doc-w1-s5): OMIT - re-probe CONTRADICTS the staged determination 'no other control character (lone CR) is a terminator': the free-form line terminator is not ONE rule. The preprocessor (ReferenceFormatProcessor.NormalizeToFreeFormMapped, directive recognition) splits lines on LF only, but the lexer ends a floating comment and a literal at a lone CR (CobolLexer.g4 COMMENT_TEXT ~[\r\n]+, STR_BODY). probe/cr3.cob, cr4.cob: 'DISPLAY "A" *> comment<CR>DISPLAY "B"' runs both A and B (the CR ended the comment); probe/cr5.cob: 'DISPLAY "A"<CR>>>DEFINE X AS 1' -> COBOL0307 unexpected '>' (the CR did NOT start a new line for the directive facility). FF and VT inside a line are COBOL0307 (cr1/cr2), i.e. not terminators. New defect proposed; PB1496 (open) owes the row once one rule exists.

defect.mechanism: Two stages answer 'what terminates a free-form line' differently: the reference-format/directive stage splits on LF only (CR before LF trimmed), while the lexer treats a lone CR as a line end for floating comments and literals. A lone CR therefore ends a *> comment but a >> directive after it is not at a line start.
defect.expected_from_spec: §6.1 3) b): the implementor shall specify THE control characters that terminate a free-form line - one set, applied by every stage (a line is a line for comments, literals and compiler directives alike).
defect.observed: cr3: comment ended at lone CR (B displayed); cr5: '>>DEFINE' after lone CR -> COBOL0307 unexpected '>'.

record.notes: A.1 item 157 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 157): required + documented (A.1 cites 'Clause 6, Reference format, rule 1c'). §6.1: 'The implementor shall specify the meaning of lines and character positions' (cite.py --check 6.1 -> OK §6.1 c)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-157 row; DOC-A.1-158 fixes only margin R (col 72) and does not say what a line or a character position IS (record vs LF-delimited line, one UTF-16 code unit vs byte per position, whether a short fixed-form record is padded to margin R). Code: a line is an LF-delimited segment of the decoded source text (CR trimmed); a character position is one char of that string; a fixed-form line's program-text area is line[7..] truncated to 65 but NEVER padded to margin R — which kb/Work PB1491 measures as a wrong answer for a continued literal (GnuCOBOL/IBM pad) — and a free-form line over the §6.1 a) 255-position maximum is accepted silently (kb/Work PB1496). Undocumented, with an edge in dispute => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning notes kb/Work PB1496 (open; its fixer owes the DOC-A.1-157 row) and PB1491 (open; the padding behaviour the row must state) — cited, not re-reported. || Writer (doc-w1-s5): OMIT - the row would have to state whether a short fixed-form record is padded to margin R, and kb/Work PB1491 (open, MAJOR, wrong_answer) measures the current no-padding answer as wrong for a continued literal; PB1496 (open) additionally owes the 255-position free-form limit. The free-form line terminator half is itself inconsistent (see the item-156 proposal). Do not document until PB1491 lands.

evidence: kb/Work PB1491 (open, wrong_answer, 'a short physical record is not padded to margin R so the continued literal loses its trailing spaces'); PB1496 (open) 'What the fixer owes: 157 must state ... that a short record is padded to margin R - PB1491 implements it'.

defect.mechanism: A fixed-form line shorter than margin R is not padded to margin R, so the meaning of character positions 8..72 of a short record is not the standard's (a continued alphanumeric literal loses its trailing spaces).
defect.expected_from_spec: §6.1 1) c) + §6.2 fixed-form margins: the character positions up to margin R are part of the line (a continued literal includes the spaces through margin R).
defect.observed: no padding; continued literal loses trailing spaces (PB1491)

row: | DOC-A.1-160 | **Report writer printable item — the fixed correspondence between columns and national characters**, §13.18.14.4 GR2, required + documented | **One column per national character position** — the same one-to-one correspondence as for an alphanumeric character. A national printable item described `PIC N(n)` (explicit or implied USAGE NATIONAL, including one inherited from a group entry) occupies exactly n columns, starting at the column its COLUMN clause names, and the horizontal counter advances by n (§13.18.14.4 GR9; `DataItem.DisplayTextWidth`, used by `ReportWriterEmitter.EmitFieldPlacements`).
